correct_completion: had I seen such a beautiful sunset.
full_sentence: Never before in my life, had I seen such a beautiful sunset.
acceptable_variants: had I ever seen such a beautiful sunset.
had I witnessed such a beautiful sunset.

options.text: I had seen such a beautiful sunset.
options.why_wrong: After a negative adverbial such as 'never before', English needs subject-auxiliary inversion for emphasis. Normal word order is incorrect here.

options.text: had I seen such a beautiful sunset.
I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
options.why_wrong: This is grammatically possible, but it has no inversion, so it does not give the emphatic structure the stem requires.

options.text: did I see such a beautiful sunset.
options.why_wrong: 'Did' is the wrong auxiliary here. The earlier past event needs the past perfect, so 'had' must be used with inversion.

grammar_focus: Inversion after negative adverbials with the past perfect
explanation: After a negative adverbial placed at the start of a clause, English moves the auxiliary 'had' in front of the subject for emphasis. Speakers often keep normal word order by habit, but this structure is required in formal and literary English.
translation: Ніколи раніше в житті я не бачив такого прекрасного заходу сонця.
